title: Working at Redwood: Careers, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools - People Ops Guide (2026 v3)
author: Ava Chen
summary: Concise People Ops handbook covering role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks summary, hiring and onboarding workflows, manager checklists, and first-step guides for core internal tools.
body:
Purpose and scope:

This People Ops guide is intended as a single-page reference for new hires, hiring managers, and people managers. It consolidates the most-used guidance: role and leveling expectations, benefits and perks summary, the hiring and onboarding workflow, manager responsibilities, and quick-start notes for internal tools. For detailed procedures and templates follow the links in the Templates & Resources section.

Section A: Roles & Career Ladders

Objective: Provide consistent language for role expectations, promotion criteria, and leveling across teams. Use the official leveling rubric stored in People Ops > Leveling for calibration details.

Canonical levels (examples used in job postings):
- IC1 / Associate: Early-career engineers or contributors (0-2 years). Focus on execution with guidance, learning core systems.
- IC2 / Engineer: Independent contributor (2-5 years). Owns features end-to-end and collaborates across teams.
- IC3 / Senior Engineer: Leads feature design, mentors others, drives medium-complexity initiatives.
- IC4 / Staff Engineer: Owns cross-team technical areas, designs large systems, and advises multiple teams.
- IC5 / Principal: Strategic technical leadership with company-wide influence.
- Manager 1 / Eng Manager: People manager of a small team (3-7), accountable for delivery and growth.
- Manager 2 / Senior Manager / Director: Manages managers or large programs; responsible for strategy, hiring, and budgets.

Promotion summary (process):
1) Initiate: Manager or individual submits promotion packet in Confluence using the Promotion Packet template.
2) Packet: impact narratives, goal outcomes, 3 supporting reviewers, evidence artifacts (PRs, metrics, designs).
3) Review: Leveling committee + People Ops evaluate against rubric, interview if needed.
4) Decision & feedback: Outcome published and manager delivers feedback and growth plan. Target turnaround: 4-6 weeks.

Key promotion signals (rubric highlights): delivery scale and quality, cross-team influence, autonomy, complexity handled, mentoring/leadership, measurable impact on product or platform metrics.

Section B: Benefits & Perks (high-level)

Health & Wellness:
- Medical (PPO/HMO), Dental, Vision plans available.
- HSA option where applicable; employee contributions pre-tax.

Time Off:
- Flexible PTO policy, 12 company holidays, and discretionary company-wide off days.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (region-specific adjustments apply).

Financial:
- 401(k) with employer match up to 4% (US).
- Competitive equity grants with periodic refresh for high-impact contributors.

Learning & Development:
- $2,000 annual L&D stipend, conference budget, internal training weeks. Manager approval required for larger requests.

Office & Remote:
- One-time home office stipend ($800), optional commuter benefits for office locations, flexible remote-first policy. See Remote Work Policy for regional guidance.

Perks:
- Monthly wellness stipend, team offsites, hardware discounts, and catered in-office events when available.

Enrollment & support: Use People Ops portal to enroll in benefits and submit claims. Open enrollment each November. For benefits questions contact benefits@redwood.com.

Section C: Hiring Principles & Interview Process

Hiring principles:
- Clear role definition: every posting must include mission, success criteria, and hiring manager.
- Structured interviews and rubrics to reduce bias.
- Timely process: target time-to-offer ~28 days for standard IC roles.

Typical interview loop (Software Engineer):
1) Recruiter screen (30min) – role fit and logistics.
2) Technical screen (45min) – algorithms, systems, or take-home.
3) Onsite / virtual loop (3-4 interviews) – coding, system design, behavioral, hiring manager.
4) Debrief & decision within 3 business days of loop.

Offer approvals: Recruiting issues offers after approvals from Hiring Manager, People Ops, and Finance. Compensation guidance and ranges are maintained in the Hiring Manager Toolkit.

Section D: Onboarding checklist (first 90 days)

Pre-start (Day 0):
- Equipment shipped, Okta enrollment invite sent, calendar invites for orientation.

Day 1:
- Company orientation (People Ops), benefits overview, team welcome and buddy intro.

Week 1:
- Access to primary systems confirmed, security training completed, dev environment setup started.

Month 1:
- Ship first small task or bugfix, establish weekly 1:1 cadence, finalize 90-day goals.

Month 3:
- 90-day check-in meeting, feedback collected, confirm long-term project assignment.

Manager responsibilities for new hires:
- Prepare a documented 30/60/90 plan and share with new hire.
- Assign a buddy and schedule recurring 1:1s.
- Ensure access to repos, monitoring dashboards, and CI/CD pipelines.
- Schedule introductions with key cross-functional partners.

Section E: Internal Tools Quick Reference

This section lists core tools and first steps. For deeper instructions search Confluence or contact infra-support@redwood.com.

Identity & Access:
- Okta SSO is required. Complete enrollment within 24 hours of start to avoid access delays. For IAM issues contact iam@redwood.com.

Docs & Knowledge:
- Confluence (confluence.redwood.internal). Request editor rights via People Ops. Bookmark team and product spaces.

Code & Collaboration:
- GitHub Enterprise (github.com/redwood). Configure SSH keys and request repo access through the repo-access form in Confluence.
- Pull request etiquette: small, well-scoped PRs with clear descriptions and linked issues.

CI/CD & Deployments:
- CircleCI + internal deployment wrappers. Common command: "deploy --env staging --service <service-name>". See eng-infra/runbooks for environment-specific details.

Messaging & Meetings:
- Slack workspace channels: #core, #eng, #product; include timezone in profile. Use huddle or call for quick syncs.

Monitoring & Incident:
- Datadog for metrics and dashboards; PagerDuty for on-call. New on-call members must complete the on-call playbook and add themselves to the team schedule.

Secrets & Keys:
- HashiCorp Vault + KMS for production secrets. Submit Secrets/Access requests via JIRA with required justification and service owners listed.

People systems:
- Greenhouse (hiring), Lattice (performance & reviews), People Ops portal (benefits, payroll).

Access escalation flow:
1) Check the relevant Confluence onboarding guide.
2) Open a ticket to infra-support@redwood.com with requested resources and role.
3) If unresolved in 48 hours, escalate to your manager and People Ops.

Section F: Manager & People Ops Reminders

- Reviews: performance reviews follow a semi-annual cadence. People Ops coordinates calibration and running the review cycle.
- Compensation: annual comp cycle in Q4 with merit and equity refresh pools; managers present comp recommendations to People Ops.
- Career conversations: managers should run structured career development check-ins twice per year.
- Code of Conduct: Redwood expects professional conduct. Report violations to hr@redwood.com.

Section G: Templates & Resources

- Promotion packet template: Confluence > People Ops > Templates.
- Detailed onboarding checklist: Confluence > People Ops > Onboarding > 90-day checklist.
- Manager 30/60/90 template: Confluence > Manager Toolkit.
- Hiring manager toolkit and compensation ranges: Confluence > Recruiting > Hiring Manager Toolkit.

Appendix: Example 30/60/90 (Engineering IC)
- 30 days: Complete dev setup, ship a bugfix, meet stakeholders.
- 60 days: Deliver a small end-to-end feature and present design to the team.
- 90 days: Improve a measurable metric (latency/cost/reliability) and outline next-quarter goals.

Ownership and maintenance
- Document owner: People Ops (Ava Chen).
- Review cadence: Annual review in January or on major policy changes.
- Edit requests: Use Confluence comments or email people-ops@redwood.com for corrections or updates.

End of People Ops guide.
